pyproject.toml: # Correctness and security rules only; style is not a CI gate.
select = ["E9", "F", "B", "S", "PLE", "W605", "PGH004"]   # PGH004: a noqa must name its rule
"B011",  # assert False in tests is deliberate
"S311",  # random is used for seeded fuzzing, never for secrets
"B904",  # explicit `raise ... from None` is used where chaining would leak
"B007",  # historical benchmark scripts keep their loop variables
"live_capture.py" = ["S603", "S404", "S607"]   # argv-only subprocess with resolved executable, reviewed
"tools/check_pin_drift.py" = ["S603"]       # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
"tools/check_release_exposure.py" = ["S603"]   # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
"tools/check_workflow_policy.py" = ["S603"]    # resolved git executable with argv-only arguments, reviewed
bandit.yaml: # Accepted findings, reviewed against THREAT-MODEL.md T8 and SR-12:
#   B404 import subprocess, B603 subprocess call without shell — live_capture.py
#   starts tcpdump with an argv list only (no shell), a resolved executable path,
#   a validated interface name and a filter that is passed as one argument.
.gitleaks.toml: # gitleaks configuration (SSDLC.md): extend the default rules, allow documented protocol test vectors.
description = "Published protocol test vectors are not credentials"
# RFC 6455 section 1.3 WebSocket example nonce/accept and RFC 9001/9369 QUIC vectors reproduced in fixtures.
